Diamond Scammer: Forever Diamonds and Gold

By: Graham Coetzer | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
What do the Sicilian Mafia, angry investors and illicit diamonds have in common? They're all connected to South African Louis Liebenberg, the man investors say has cheated them out of millions .

Unique Selling Point:
Louis Petrus Liebenberg is a self proclaimed diamond king - the son of a pastor who grew up on the diamonds fields of the west coast in Port Nolloth, Liebenberg claims he is a specialist in the field and currently offers investors in his business Forever Gold and Diamonds returns of between 50% to 100% within 14, 21 or 30 days, supposedly possible by buying small packages of uncut diamonds. The only problem is, very few of the investors ever seem to have received any of the promised returns on their investments. What's worse, they've never even seen their initial capital back either. But this is not the first time Louis has gotten away with taking in millions for investments and failing to return on his promises. In 2005, Liebenberg opened Wealth4U mining and Exploration, raking in at least R130 million in investments from 1700 shareholders. But by 2009 the company was liquidated, and the only assets worth anything amounted to a poorly R7 million - investors lost everything.

Summary:
We have been approached by several investors, one of them who sank R3.2 million into Liebenberg's promised deals and has never seen a scent back, who all say Louis is living the high life in a luxury house in an estate in Bronkhorstpruit off their money. He is constantly bringing in new investors, but we have found none who have actually received any of the promised returns or their initial money back. When they start pressuring Louis for their money, he scares them off in three ways: 1. He threatens that if people approach the media, the company will collapse as Wealth4U did and he will liquidate and no one will see any money, 2: he says he is dealing illegally in diamonds and they are therefore implicated, 3: he comes up with threatening stories about the underworld, gangsters he knows, hits put out on peoples lives etc. We have documentary proof of all of the above via facebook posts, whatsapp messages, etc. From videos that Liebenberg himself makes as marketing material, it is clear that he makes the deals sound legit, he says its done under legal certificates etc, SO INVESTORS ARE NOT INITIALLY AWARE THAT HIS DEALINGS ARE ILLEGAL.

Further information:
-We have many videos of Liebenberg where he records himself making offers to investors, and also where he behaves very erratically, aggressively when stories questioning his business are covered in the media.

- We have Facebook posts where Liebenberg admits he is trading in diamonds illegally - justifying it by saying that government and De Beers are in cahoots and preventing the ordinary South African from their rights to trade in Diamonds.

- We have surveillance footage(video and pics) from a source of Liebenberg leading a meeting of illegal diggers at the Kleinzee mining area

- We have Liebenberg admitting that he is the leader of these diggers, and that he is funding their court bid to have their operations legalised. We have newspaper articles where he is at one of the court appearances.

-We have whatsapp voice notes between Liebenberg and investors where he repeatedly comes up with excuses on why the promised returns, in one case 250% returns, are not being paid.

-We have three case studies, one of them who spent R3.2 million, the other two both hundreds of thousands of rands, who have never received a scent back. All three are willing to do on camera interviews.

-We have several articles, including a Mail and Guardian report, detailing the Wealth4U debacle, the mafia involvement, and the involvement of known La Cosa Nostra banker Victor Pallazolo who operated in South Africa at the time, before being sentenced to jail in Italy.

-We have recent marketing videos Louis has made, where he markets the diamond investments to Afrikaners from the Eureka town(Eureka is the whites only settlement planned in Namakwaland by another well known fraudster, Adriaan Niewoudt, also known as Adriaan Vrotmelk, who in the '80s took many millions of rands from SA investors in scam involving milk cultures known at the time as Kubus) It is not clear if the two are working together, although Liebenberg has posted that he is buying land in Eureka.

Extra Budget Items:
JUST SOME EXTRA NOTES AND POSSIBLE CONCERNS:

Liebenberg might play the "investors knew they were buying into an illegal investment scheme" card
He might get some sympathy on the uplifting the people of Namakwaland, the Namas, from the evil state and De Beers.
He is known to be litigious
Many of the possible case studies are all over the country and would require lots of travelling, but two are doable. Hennie who lost R3.2mill is in Ermelo, Michael who lost R350 000 is in JHB.
We have emailed Liebenberg and asked him for an interview, he has yet to respond.

Script:


Diamonds are Forever / Louis Liebenberg
2nd Draft Script
31 March 2020


Voice
This is Louis Petrus Liebenberg. The controversial 55 year-old businessman has earned himself a rather notorious reputation in the South African diamond industry. His Forever Gold and Diamonds business, promoted via social media, offers people incredible returns on their investments.

Sound Up “Mandy”
He asked people to invest in his project.

Voice
The deal sounds simple - investors buy into parcels of uncut diamonds like the ones seen posted here. Liebenberg gets them from undisclosed sources in the diamond rich areas of South Africa’s west coast and Namakwaland. In offers like this one Liebenberg says: “We make approximately 50% profit every ten days by buying and selling without any cutting done. 100% plus when we cut.” The 50% return is offered over a 14 day time period and the 100% return takes 30 days.

Link Derek
Louis Liebenberg has a long history in the diamond industry, and one thing he’s very good at is raising money from investors.

Voice
Mandy, not her real name as she’s asked us to hide her identity, says the Facebook offers were very tempting.

Sound Up “Mandy”
Derek: What did he offer you?

Mandy: He said that you could get two to three times what you initially invested.

Voice
After receiving double her money back from Liebenberg on a small R5000 test run, Mandy and a group of friends invested a second time.

Sound Up Mandy
And then there was a second opportunity, but then I had some friends that were interested, and in total we invested about half a million rand.

Voice
But two years later they haven’t received a cent from Liebenberg.

Sound Up Mandy
So he did ask me to invest more, because he needed more money, but I said no Louis, I’m not going to do that, I’m not going to invest anything unless you’ve paid.

Link Derek
We’ve come to Ermelo to meet one of the investors, Hennie Nieuwenhuis, who’s been running a glass and aluminium fitting business in this Mpumalanga town for the past 24 years.

Sound Up Hennie
Derek: What sort of returns was he offering?

Hennie: Double and more.

Derek: Double and more in what time?

Hennie: 10 to 14 days.

Voice
Libenberg told him he was buying the diamonds from the Nama people of the Namaqualand and Richtersveld areas of South Africa.

Sound Up Hennie
And there’s the coloured people, getting diamonds, bringing it to him. He buys it from them and then sells it at a profit.

Voice
Liebenberg calls himself an activist for the plight of the Nama people, descendants of the KhoiKhoi, many of whom live in abject poverty. When big diamond miners like De Beers, a huge source of jobs to the Namas, scaled down their operations along the West Coast, some Nama’s turned to illegal mining to support themselves - bringing them into conflict with the authorities.

Sound Up Protest footage and singing
What did we do?

Voice
Nieuwenhuis says he started off with a R50 000 investment, and when Liebenberg told him they’d made a profit on the first parcel of diamonds, Hennie was happy to reinvest it.

Sound Up Hennie
Eventually I want him to give me a return.

Voice
Over the following weeks Liebenberg kept offering Nieuwenhuis opportunities to invest in new parcels, each time promising high returns.

Sound Up Hennie
We can buy for R50 000 and sell for R120 000…

Voice
Before he realised how far he’d gone, Nieuwenhuis says he’d handed over millions in just a few months.

Sound Up Hennie
Derek: So how much did you lose?

Hennie: Almost R3,2 million.

Derek: In that short time?

Hennie: In that short time.

Derek: So just tell us how that happened?

Hennie: No, well he’s so convincing. As I say, every time, the carrot is in front of you.

Derek: But these are diamonds carrots?

Hennie: These are diamond carrots ja. I’m still waiting for my double money.

Voice
While investors say Liebenberg’s left them in the lurch, he seems to be leading a life of luxury at his upmarket house in a gated community in Bronkhorstpruit just outside of Pretoria, complete with spectacular views of the dam.

Sound Up Louis
Derek: We’ve seen offers to investors, where you offer them five times return…

Louis: But you can do it.

Derek: In 21 days?

Louis: Yes.

Derek: You can do it, but it hasn’t been done.

Louis: Ok, what I’m doing at the moment, I’m not doing that. I’m saying to them, I guess, not guess, I estimate, that we can make on this stone, or on this parcel, so much. But I also tell them it could be zero. It could be zero. But the exercise that I’ve gone through…

Derek: You don’t always tell them they’re taking a gamble Louis.

Louis: I do tell them that they’re taking a gamble.

Derek: Not on every video.

Voice
Liebenberg sends potential investors home made videos like these.

Sound Up Louis cellphone video
So on the short term parcels, you’ll get profit of anything from 30% to 100% and possible more.

Voice
But just like many of his Facebook offers, the videos don’t always spell out the risks.

Sound Up Louis
Louis:I mean I’m a salesman Derek…

Derek: You are

Louis: I’m not going to tell people that you know, you’re going to see your arse, but then nobody will do anything. If we get the diamonds, if we get the permits in Namaqualand, you know we’re going to make billions.

Voice
Liebenberg, seen here addressing a group of artisinal miners in the diamond rich town of Kleinzee, has joined forces with one of the self proclaimed chiefs of the Nama people, Paul Swartbooi to lobby government to grant the Namas mining permits. While negotiations and court cases continue, towns like Kleinzee have been overrun by diggers who illegally mine there.

Sound Up Louis
Why don’t they want to give Kleinzee, why don’t they want to give Langhoogte, Tweepad, all those areas to people that’s been there for hundreds of years.


Voice
In South Africa it is illegal for the public to trade in or even have in their possession uncut diamonds, and questions have been raised about the legality of Liebenberg’s dealings.

Sound Up Louis
Derek: Are you currently registered as a diamond dealer?

Louis: No, I’m not interested, I’ve got many associations with diamond dealers… So let me tell you something Derek. In South Africa, 95% of all diamond dealing is illegal.

Derek: So is your dealing legal or illegal?

Louis: Both. But we make it legal.

Voice
He admits that he’s used large sums of the money raised from investors on funding court cases for the Nama’s and he’s own expenses.

Sound Up Louis
We’ve got a 164 investors, we’ve got a total of R9.3 million that invested, I’ve paid out R3.6 million. I’ve spent about R6 million on either fighting for the Namas and own expenses, travelling, staying, whatever. You know as I said earlier how much must I earn.

Voice
Which would mean that, by his own admission, rather than doubling the R9 million of investors money he claims to have raised, he’s spent about two thirds of it.

Sound Up Louis
Derek: How many investors do you owe money to right now?

Louis: Of the 164, I won’t be able to give you a figure, I must be honest I don’t know, I’ll look into it and I’ll give you the data.

Derek: You should know.

Louis: But yes, no, no how? You owe some of the money, I’ve paid some of the money. I’ll pay the rest.

Voice
Liebenberg often blames the media for scaring away his investors. In this bizarre video clip posted on social media, he’s seen impersonating an afrikaans journalist who questioned his diamond dealings.

Sound Up Louis Videos
Louis: There are swindlers and scoundrels all over the fucking world, you’ll find them across the world Kittie, they are such unbelievably wonderful people. And they will take all your things, your intestines, your kidneys, your backside.

Sound Up Louis
Louis: Derek…

Derek: That was quite a rant though?

Louis: Yes it is. I love that, I love that. I did Scrooge, A Christmas Carol with Hannes Muller on stage, and maybe I’m a bit of an actor as well, because life is an act. This is not true, this is virtual reality, it’s not real.

Voice
What is real, is this isn’t the first time Louis has lost investors money. In 2009, his Marine diamond mining company Wealth4U cost investors millions.

Sound Up Louis
In Wealth4U I collected R156 million from people, going from hotel to hotel.

Link Derek
But despite the millions he raised setting up Wealth4U, the money didn’t end up in investors pockets.

Voice
Wealth4U was started in 2004, and the funds raised were supposed to be used to mine diamonds offshore. Investors were offered 5% per month return on their investments.

Sound Up Michael Roberts
It did look good, I mean Louis is a brilliant salesman, and he gave his pitch

Voice
Michael Roberts from Cape Town invested in Wealth4U in 2007.

Sound Up Michael
I put in 600K (R600 000)

Voice
But just two years later the money was gone and the company liquidated, with the assets at the time reportedly only worth about R7 million.

Sound Up Michael
I have not received one scent from Louis Liebenberg. Nothing.

Voice
Liebenberg says Wealth4U’s woes started with the Global Financial crisis in 2008.

Sound Up Louis
So our business was right, but our timing was totally out.

Voice
In this Mail and Guardian article from 2015, it was revealed that Liebenberg had ties to the Sicilian mafia during his Wealth4U days. Louis says the mob had offered to help fund the floundering Wealth4U.

Sound Up Louis
And then the Sicilian Mafia came and they said they’ll give me R10 million, I must offer the rest of my assets, and I did that. But then they did not come up with the R10 million, they only came up with R2 million, and I couldn’t crack it again, I just couldn’t get started.

Voice
But while many investors lost their money, Liebenberg made himself a tidy bundle.

Sound Up Louis
Derek: Simple question Louis, what did you leave Wealth4U with in terms of capital?

Louis: Ok, I’ll tell you what, I got R30 million rand in the prospectus, being the founder of that… So I had R30 million. I bought farms, I bought racehorses, because I wanted to sit next to Mrs Oppenheimer, because I wanted to feel like how it is to have money, because I grew up like, pretty poor.

Voice
He’s promised to pay everyone back, and is now taking on new investors - this time from the people of the Eureka movement. Eureka is the exclusively white community started by Adriaan Nieuwoudt in the Northern Cape, and Liebenberg says with the capital he raises from them his company will finally be a success.

Sound Up Louis
Because Eureka understands this, because those people look at the future, whats happening now, the cash is coming in. The cash is coming in and I’m buying. And because I’m buying, I’m paying. And because I’m paying, more people will come.

Voice
Liebenberg has convinced Nieuwoudt, who ran an infamous milk cultures pyramid scheme in South Africa in the 1980’s called Kubus, to work with him and the Namas.
And he’s not concerned about his people investing in Liebenberg’s diamond parcels.

Sound Up Adriaan
Of Eureka’s people, not one person has lost a cent. What happened previously with other people, I really can’t say.

Voice
Little consolation to investors like Hennie Nieuwenhuis, who has had to indefinitely postpone his retirement plans and sell some of his properties to cover his losses.

Sound Up Hennie
So i decided to keep on with the business, to keep on for another couple of years.



Promo 1
Voice
Would you invest your cash with a controversial businessman who offers to double your money buying and selling uncut diamonds? We meet people who say they did, and lost millions.

Promo 2
Voice
Illegal diamond mining on the west coast, the Sicilian Mafia and investors left in the lurch. A bizarre story about a controversial businessman who’s raised millions from the public.

Promo 3
Voice
It sounds too good to be true, a diamond dealer offering the public double their money on investments. But many have been left out of pocket, saying he owes them millions.

Last Updated 12 April 2020 - Carte Blanche HD mihle@combinedartists.co.za 11 June 2020 Script: Diamonds are Forever / Louis Liebenberg 2nd Draft Script 31 March 2020 Voice This is Louis Petrus Liebenberg. The controversial 55 year-old businessman has earned himself a rather notorious reputation in the South African diamond industry. His Forever Gold and Diamonds business, promoted via social media, offers people incredible returns on their investments. Sound Up “Mandy” He asked people to invest in his project. Voice The deal sounds simple - investors buy into parcels of uncut diamonds like the ones seen posted here. Liebenberg gets them from undisclosed sources in the diamond rich areas of South Africa’s west coast and Namakwaland. In offers like this one Liebenberg says: “We make approximately 50% profit every ten days by buying and selling without any cutting done. 100% plus when we cut.” The 50% return is offered over a 14 day time period and the 100% return takes 30 days. Link Derek Louis Liebenberg has a long history in the diamond industry, and one thing he’s very good at is raising money from investors. Voice Mandy, not her real name as she’s asked us to hide her identity, says the Facebook offers were very tempting. Sound Up “Mandy” Derek: What did he offer you? Mandy: He said that you could get two to three times what you initially invested. Voice After receiving double her money back from Liebenberg on a small R5000 test run, Mandy and a group of friends invested a second time. Sound Up Mandy And then there was a second opportunity, but then I had some friends that were interested, and in total we invested about half a million rand. Voice But two years later they haven’t received a cent from Liebenberg. Sound Up Mandy So he did ask me to invest more, because he needed more money, but I said no Louis, I’m not going to do that, I’m not going to invest anything unless you’ve paid. Link Derek We’ve come to Ermelo to meet one of the investors, Hennie Nieuwenhuis, who’s been running a glass and aluminium fitting business in this Mpumalanga town for the past 24 years. Sound Up Hennie Derek: What sort of returns was he offering? Hennie: Double and more. Derek: Double and more in what time? Hennie: 10 to 14 days. Voice Libenberg told him he was buying the diamonds from the Nama people of the Namaqualand and Richtersveld areas of South Africa. Sound Up Hennie And there’s the coloured people, getting diamonds, bringing it to him. He buys it from them and then sells it at a profit. Voice Liebenberg calls himself an activist for the plight of the Nama people, descendants of the KhoiKhoi, many of whom live in abject poverty. When big diamond miners like De Beers, a huge source of jobs to the Namas, scaled down their operations along the West Coast, some Nama’s turned to illegal mining to support themselves - bringing them into conflict with the authorities. Sound Up Protest footage and singing What did we do? Voice Nieuwenhuis says he started off with a R50 000 investment, and when Liebenberg told him they’d made a profit on the first parcel of diamonds, Hennie was happy to reinvest it. Sound Up Hennie Eventually I want him to give me a return. Voice Over the following weeks Liebenberg kept offering Nieuwenhuis opportunities to invest in new parcels, each time promising high returns. Sound Up Hennie We can buy for R50 000 and sell for R120 000… Voice Before he realised how far he’d gone, Nieuwenhuis says he’d handed over millions in just a few months. Sound Up Hennie Derek: So how much did you lose? Hennie: Almost R3,2 million. Derek: In that short time? Hennie: In that short time. Derek: So just tell us how that happened? Hennie: No, well he’s so convincing. As I say, every time, the carrot is in front of you. Derek: But these are diamonds carrots? Hennie: These are diamond carrots ja. I’m still waiting for my double money. Voice While investors say Liebenberg’s left them in the lurch, he seems to be leading a life of luxury at his upmarket house in a gated community in Bronkhorstpruit just outside of Pretoria, complete with spectacular views of the dam. Sound Up Louis Derek: We’ve seen offers to investors, where you offer them five times return… Louis: But you can do it. Derek: In 21 days? Louis: Yes. Derek: You can do it, but it hasn’t been done. Louis: Ok, what I’m doing at the moment, I’m not doing that. I’m saying to them, I guess, not guess, I estimate, that we can make on this stone, or on this parcel, so much. But I also tell them it could be zero. It could be zero. But the exercise that I’ve gone through… Derek: You don’t always tell them they’re taking a gamble Louis. Louis: I do tell them that they’re taking a gamble. Derek: Not on every video. Voice Liebenberg sends potential investors home made videos like these. Sound Up Louis cellphone video So on the short term parcels, you’ll get profit of anything from 30% to 100% and possible more. Voice But just like many of his Facebook offers, the videos don’t always spell out the risks. Sound Up Louis Louis:I mean I’m a salesman Derek… Derek: You are Louis: I’m not going to tell people that you know, you’re going to see your arse, but then nobody will do anything. If we get the diamonds, if we get the permits in Namaqualand, you know we’re going to make billions. Voice Liebenberg, seen here addressing a group of artisinal miners in the diamond rich town of Kleinzee, has joined forces with one of the self proclaimed chiefs of the Nama people, Paul Swartbooi to lobby government to grant the Namas mining permits. While negotiations and court cases continue, towns like Kleinzee have been overrun by diggers who illegally mine there. Sound Up Louis Why don’t they want to give Kleinzee, why don’t they want to give Langhoogte, Tweepad, all those areas to people that’s been there for hundreds of years. Voice In South Africa it is illegal for the public to trade in or even have in their possession uncut diamonds, and questions have been raised about the legality of Liebenberg’s dealings. Sound Up Louis Derek: Are you currently registered as a diamond dealer? Louis: No, I’m not interested, I’ve got many associations with diamond dealers… So let me tell you something Derek. In South Africa, 95% of all diamond dealing is illegal. Derek: So is your dealing legal or illegal? Louis: Both. But we make it legal. Voice He admits that he’s used large sums of the money raised from investors on funding court cases for the Nama’s and he’s own expenses. Sound Up Louis We’ve got a 164 investors, we’ve got a total of R9.3 million that invested, I’ve paid out R3.6 million. I’ve spent about R6 million on either fighting for the Namas and own expenses, travelling, staying, whatever. You know as I said earlier how much must I earn. Voice Which would mean that, by his own admission, rather than doubling the R9 million of investors money he claims to have raised, he’s spent about two thirds of it. Sound Up Louis Derek: How many investors do you owe money to right now? Louis: Of the 164, I won’t be able to give you a figure, I must be honest I don’t know, I’ll look into it and I’ll give you the data. Derek: You should know. Louis: But yes, no, no how? You owe some of the money, I’ve paid some of the money. I’ll pay the rest. Voice Liebenberg often blames the media for scaring away his investors. In this bizarre video clip posted on social media, he’s seen impersonating an afrikaans journalist who questioned his diamond dealings. Sound Up Louis Videos Louis: There are swindlers and scoundrels all over the fucking world, you’ll find them across the world Kittie, they are such unbelievably wonderful people. And they will take all your things, your intestines, your kidneys, your backside. Sound Up Louis Louis: Derek… Derek: That was quite a rant though? Louis: Yes it is. I love that, I love that. I did Scrooge, A Christmas Carol with Hannes Muller on stage, and maybe I’m a bit of an actor as well, because life is an act. This is not true, this is virtual reality, it’s not real. Voice What is real, is this isn’t the first time Louis has lost investors money. In 2009, his Marine diamond mining company Wealth4U cost investors millions. Sound Up Louis In Wealth4U I collected R156 million from people, going from hotel to hotel. Link Derek But despite the millions he raised setting up Wealth4U, the money didn’t end up in investors pockets. Voice Wealth4U was started in 2004, and the funds raised were supposed to be used to mine diamonds offshore. Investors were offered 5% per month return on their investments. Sound Up Michael Roberts It did look good, I mean Louis is a brilliant salesman, and he gave his pitch Voice Michael Roberts from Cape Town invested in Wealth4U in 2007. Sound Up Michael I put in 600K (R600 000) Voice But just two years later the money was gone and the company liquidated, with the assets at the time reportedly only worth about R7 million. Sound Up Michael I have not received one scent from Louis Liebenberg. Nothing. Voice Liebenberg says Wealth4U’s woes started with the Global Financial crisis in 2008. Sound Up Louis So our business was right, but our timing was totally out. Voice In this Mail and Guardian article from 2015, it was revealed that Liebenberg had ties to the Sicilian mafia during his Wealth4U days. Louis says the mob had offered to help fund the floundering Wealth4U. Sound Up Louis And then the Sicilian Mafia came and they said they’ll give me R10 million, I must offer the rest of my assets, and I did that. But then they did not come up with the R10 million, they only came up with R2 million, and I couldn’t crack it again, I just couldn’t get started. Voice But while many investors lost their money, Liebenberg made himself a tidy bundle. Sound Up Louis Derek: Simple question Louis, what did you leave Wealth4U with in terms of capital? Louis: Ok, I’ll tell you what, I got R30 million rand in the prospectus, being the founder of that… So I had R30 million. I bought farms, I bought racehorses, because I wanted to sit next to Mrs Oppenheimer, because I wanted to feel like how it is to have money, because I grew up like, pretty poor. Voice He’s promised to pay everyone back, and is now taking on new investors - this time from the people of the Eureka movement. Eureka is the exclusively white community started by Adriaan Nieuwoudt in the Northern Cape, and Liebenberg says with the capital he raises from them his company will finally be a success. Sound Up Louis Because Eureka understands this, because those people look at the future, whats happening now, the cash is coming in. The cash is coming in and I’m buying. And because I’m buying, I’m paying. And because I’m paying, more people will come. Voice Liebenberg has convinced Nieuwoudt, who ran an infamous milk cultures pyramid scheme in South Africa in the 1980’s called Kubus, to work with him and the Namas. And he’s not concerned about his people investing in Liebenberg’s diamond parcels. Sound Up Adriaan Of Eureka’s people, not one person has lost a cent. What happened previously with other people, I really can’t say. Voice Little consolation to investors like Hennie Nieuwenhuis, who has had to indefinitely postpone his retirement plans and sell some of his properties to cover his losses. Sound Up Hennie So i decided to keep on with the business, to keep on for another couple of years. Promo 1 Voice Would you invest your cash with a controversial businessman who offers to double your money buying and selling uncut diamonds? We meet people who say they did, and lost millions. Promo 2 Voice Illegal diamond mining on the west coast, the Sicilian Mafia and investors left in the lurch. A bizarre story about a controversial businessman who’s raised millions from the public. Promo 3 Voice It sounds too good to be true, a diamond dealer offering the public double their money on investments. But many have been left out of pocket, saying he owes them millions.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): What do the Sicilian Mafia, angry investors and illicit diamonds have in common? They're all connected to South African Louis Liebenberg, the man investors say has cheated them out of millions .
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Louis Petrus Liebenberg is a self proclaimed diamond king - the son of a pastor who grew up on the diamonds fields of the west coast in Port Nolloth, Liebenberg claims he is a specialist in the field and currently offers investors in his business Forever Gold and Diamonds returns of between 50% to 100% within 14, 21 or 30 days, supposedly possible by buying small packages of uncut diamonds. The only problem is, very few of the investors ever seem to have received any of the promised returns on their investments. What's worse, they've never even seen their initial capital back either. But this is not the first time Louis has gotten away with taking in millions for investments and failing to return on his promises. In 2005, Liebenberg opened Wealth4U mining and Exploration, raking in at least R130 million in investments from 1700 shareholders. But by 2009 the company was liquidated, and the only assets worth anything amounted to a poorly R7 million - investors lost everything.
metadata.Summary: We have been approached by several investors, one of them who sank R3.2 million into Liebenberg's promised deals and has never seen a scent back, who all say Louis is living the high life in a luxury house in an estate in Bronkhorstpruit off their money. He is constantly bringing in new investors, but we have found none who have actually received any of the promised returns or their initial money back. When they start pressuring Louis for their money, he scares them off in three ways: 1. He threatens that if people approach the media, the company will collapse as Wealth4U did and he will liquidate and no one will see any money, 2: he says he is dealing illegally in diamonds and they are therefore implicated, 3: he comes up with threatening stories about the underworld, gangsters he knows, hits put out on peoples lives etc. We have documentary proof of all of the above via facebook posts, whatsapp messages, etc. From videos that Liebenberg himself makes as marketing material, it is clear that he makes the deals sound legit, he says its done under legal certificates etc, SO INVESTORS ARE NOT INITIALLY AWARE THAT HIS DEALINGS ARE ILLEGAL.
metadata.Further information: -We have many videos of Liebenberg where he records himself making offers to investors, and also where he behaves very erratically, aggressively when stories questioning his business are covered in the media. - We have Facebook posts where Liebenberg admits he is trading in diamonds illegally - justifying it by saying that government and De Beers are in cahoots and preventing the ordinary South African from their rights to trade in Diamonds. - We have surveillance footage(video and pics) from a source of Liebenberg leading a meeting of illegal diggers at the Kleinzee mining area - We have Liebenberg admitting that he is the leader of these diggers, and that he is funding their court bid to have their operations legalised. We have newspaper articles where he is at one of the court appearances. -We have whatsapp voice notes between Liebenberg and investors where he repeatedly comes up with excuses on why the promised returns, in one case 250% returns, are not being paid. -We have three case studies, one of them who spent R3.2 million, the other two both hundreds of thousands of rands, who have never received a scent back. All three are willing to do on camera interviews. -We have several articles, including a Mail and Guardian report, detailing the Wealth4U debacle, the mafia involvement, and the involvement of known La Cosa Nostra banker Victor Pallazolo who operated in South Africa at the time, before being sentenced to jail in Italy. -We have recent marketing videos Louis has made, where he markets the diamond investments to Afrikaners from the Eureka town(Eureka is the whites only settlement planned in Namakwaland by another well known fraudster, Adriaan Niewoudt, also known as Adriaan Vrotmelk, who in the '80s took many millions of rands from SA investors in scam involving milk cultures known at the time as Kubus) It is not clear if the two are working together, although Liebenberg has posted that he is buying land in Eureka.
metadata.Extra Budget Items: JUST SOME EXTRA NOTES AND POSSIBLE CONCERNS: Liebenberg might play the "investors knew they were buying into an illegal investment scheme" card He might get some sympathy on the uplifting the people of Namakwaland, the Namas, from the evil state and De Beers. He is known to be litigious Many of the possible case studies are all over the country and would require lots of travelling, but two are doable. Hennie who lost R3.2mill is in Ermelo, Michael who lost R350 000 is in JHB. We have emailed Liebenberg and asked him for an interview, he has yet to respond.
